newsitem.title: USA: US should punish Wall St muni "fraud"-LA authority.
newsitem.headline: US should punish Wall St muni "fraud"-LA authority.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority urged U.S. regulators to seek recovery from Wall Street "wrongdoers" at bond firms who allegedly exploited localities nationwide by up to $1 billion in "yield burning fraud."

In a 43-page comment letter to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), the authority said the $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been rocked by allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond financing transactions.

The practice is known as "yield burning" becasue a bond firm charging higher prices than it paid for the Treasuries can avoid breaking federal restrictions on "arbitrage" profits while still forcing the municipality or other issuer to accept a lower yield on the Treasuries.

The IRS in July announced a process by which localities that paid more than fair market value for the Treasury securities they placed into bond escrows can avoid having interest on their bonds declared taxable by IRS.

But the LA authority said, "It was the Wall Street firms - not the municipal issuers - that knowingly misrepresented that escrow securities were priced at fair market value ... and profited handsomely."
It charged that "State and local governments were exploited and deceived precisely so Wall Street banks could enrich themselves" by as much as $1 billion.

The authority warned that requiring cities and counties to pay back Wall Street's profits would have "dire consequences" for localities nationwide, in comments that were prepared by its lawyers Phillips & Cohen in Washington.
The L.A. authority urged the Securities and Exchange Commission, Justice Department and IRS to focus their enforcement efforts on "culpable parties."
